content.text: Teams message asks whether there is an ongoing issue at Haslet, indicating incident awareness had begun.
Site reported the issue involved their ACB system and that under zone 5 they were unable to get a pair.
Site had earlier issues with a low battery AMR; attempted replacement AMRs were going to the hospital lane. Linked to the site's description of pairing problems.
Harvey suggested the robots may not have been removed and added properly, causing tasking problems, and stated the low battery was not the current issue but may have started the problem.
Site attempted to add two AGVs, one of which was underneath the rack.
When robots are removed and added, they have to be swung through the hospital to return.
Site attempted and/or had removed the AGVs they tried to add.
RMS web UI screenshots show abnormal table entries (some red-highlighted) and a note that site removed robot 158 from the system. Exact table values and before/after state unclear due to garbled OCR.
Tony on site removed robot 158; site removed robot 158 from the system, currently on charger.
Robot 153 was still reporting no charging and could still be stuck in zone 5 while trying to go charge after losing its QR code.
Site believed removing robot 158 may have fixed the issue, the system had begun working, and staff remained on the call to monitor.
Case 00228723 created for 'ACB System Down,' Type Malfunction, Priority 2-High: Production seriously impacted.
Case status: New -> In Progress -> Escalated -> Resolved.
Case status updated In Progress -> Escalated at 8:30 PM.
Case status updated Escalated -> Resolved at 9:20 PM.
Case closed at 9:20 PM.
Case closure notification sent; case opened 7:36 PM, resolved 3/13/2026.
Internal message (3/17/2026) shared a work order detail page for the Haslet hub.
Case 00228723 created for 'ACB System Down,' Priority 2-High: Production seriously impacted (Salesforce case activity).

Site removed robot 158, currently on charger. Tony reported that after removing robot 158, the system began functioning again. Monitoring continued ~10 minutes and the system remained operational before the call ended.
High-priority case summary: ACB System Down, zone 5 unable to get a pair, AMR low battery under the rack, site replaced the AMR, every AMR goes to the hospital.
Case summary (narrative): zone 5 unable to get a pair; AMR low battery under the rack; site replaced the AMR; every AMR goes to the hospital.
Resolution details: 'Site removed robot 158, which was shown to not be mapped.'
Case resolution details state robot 158 was not mapped.

'After doing so, the ECB system was reported to be functional again.' Note: source uses 'ECB system' here vs. 'ACB System Down' in the case subject -- naming inconsistency preserved from the source, not resolved.
Work order problem description references conveyor/sorting equipment emergency breakdown and an ACB needing repair in zone 5.
Use this path when a site reports that an ACB or zone cannot obtain an AMR pair, multiple AMRs route unexpectedly, or the system appears down after an AMR replacement or add/remove event.

structured_payload.title: AMR pairing failure with abnormal fleet roster or mapping state
structured_payload.user_facing_summary: Use this path when a site reports that an ACB or zone cannot obtain an AMR pair, multiple AMRs route unexpectedly, or the system appears down after an AMR replacement or add/remove event.
structured_payload.playbook_goal: Determine whether the pairing failure is associated with an abnormal AMR roster or mapping state, use an authorized site-side isolation or removal procedure when supported, and confirm that normal pairing and operation return.
observed_entry_symptoms: A site reports that an ACB or affected zone cannot get a pair.
The ACB system is described as down or production is seriously impacted.
Replacement AMRs reportedly route to the hospital lane instead of supporting the affected workflow.
An AMR was previously reported with low battery or in an abnormal physical location.
The issue follows an AMR replacement, add, or remove activity.

structured_payload.confidence_reason: The packet contains a clear observable symptom, a named RMS surface, discussion of possible roster/add-remove behavior, a source-supported site removal action, and reported recovery. Confidence is limited because the RMS details are partly unreadable, recovery was reported rather than independently measured, and the source contains inconsistent ACB/ECB naming.

nodes.title: Confirm the observable pairing and routing pattern
nodes.intent: Determine whether the site is experiencing an active pairing failure with abnormal AMR routing or behavior after a replacement or add/remove event.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the site is experiencing an active pairing failure with abnormal AMR routing or behavior after a replacement or add/remove event.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to interview the site about the affected zone's pairing availability, intended AMR routing, recent replacement or add/remove activity, and current physical robot behavior; this is an evidence-collection and interpretation aid, not a case-intake procedure.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source records site-reported inability to get a pair, replacement AMRs going to the hospital lane, and earlier low-battery and robot-location circumstances.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to interview the site about the affected zone's pairing availability, intended AMR routing, recent replacement or add/remove activity, and current physical robot behavior; this is an evidence-collection and interpretation aid, not a case-intake procedure.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator or L1 support confirms through site interview or visual observation whether the affected zone cannot obtain a pair, whether AMRs are routing to the hospital lane instead of the intended workflow, and whether the pattern followed an AMR replacement or add/remove event. Healthy means pairing and intended routing are available; unhealthy means pairing remains unavailable or multiple AMRs show the reported abnormal routing; inconclusive means the site cannot confirm the affected workflow, timing, or current behavior.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Support messages record a phone conversation with the site and site-reported pairing, low-battery, replacement, and hospital-lane behavior (case_228723:page_1; case_228723:page_2).

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The source describes replacement/add activity, a robot reportedly not mapped, and abnormal routing.

ontology_gaps: No ontology-backed source mapping is provided for interpreting the phrase 'unable to get a pair' from the site interview alone.
healthy_indicators: Site reports that the affected workflow can obtain a pair.
AMRs are routing to the intended workflow rather than uniformly to the hospital lane.
unhealthy_indicators: Site confirms the affected zone still cannot obtain a pair.
Multiple replacement AMRs continue routing to the hospital lane.
A recent add/remove or replacement event coincides with the current failure.
inconclusive_indicators: The site cannot reproduce the pairing failure.
The affected workflow or current robot behavior cannot be identified.

nodes.primary_action: Interview the site (and/or visually confirm) whether the affected zone still cannot obtain a pair, whether AMRs are routing to the hospital lane unexpectedly, and whether this pattern began after the reported AMR replacement/add/remove activity.
evidence_to_collect: Affected zone/workflow identifier (as described by site) and which “intended routing” they expect
Site confirmation of current pairing availability: can the zone obtain a pair right now?
Site confirmation of abnormal routing: are AMRs going to the hospital lane instead of the intended workflow?
Timeline evidence: whether the pattern coincided with the reported replacement/add/remove event (and what was changed)
Current physical/operational observation the site can report (e.g., where robots are physically behaving/standing)
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Site confirms pairing is available and AMRs route to the intended workflow rather than uniformly to the hospital lane.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Site confirms pairing remains unavailable and/or multiple replacement AMRs continue routing to the hospital lane; pattern coincides with the reported add/remove/replacement activity.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Site cannot reproduce or confirm the affected workflow, timing, or current routing/pairing behavior.

optional_corroboration.note: Do not treat site statements about low battery or hospital routing as root cause until the fleet/roster mapping is verified on RMS/WCS surfaces.

nodes.generated_guidance: Use this node to verify that the incident matches the intended observable pattern (active pairing failure + abnormal routing pattern after replacement/add/remove). If the site cannot confirm the observable pattern, do not proceed to roster-recovery actions based on assumptions.

ontology_evidence.title: WCS model — CellCodeDatabaseModel
ontology_evidence.text: Model CellCodeDatabaseModel (robotics): Stores all cell codes in the map. When a new AGV is added to the system while in a running state, the system first checks if the AGV's current cell code is in a missing zone under the sorter; if not, it uses this table to look up which hospital the cell code is connected to and sends an Initialize command to Geek.. Fields: CellCode: Cell/node code analogous to an RMS node code (vendor-agnostic).; X: X coordinate for the cell code.; Y: Y coordinate for the

ontology_evidence.title: WCS model — RobotDatabaseModel

source_refs.note: PascalCase model inventory; live query screenshot on p.77 supplied the full column list and example values

ontology_evidence.text: Model RobotDatabaseModel (robotics): Robot/AGV live state: contains the data for every robot in the system including its state, tote name, assigned sorter side, current/destination location, and state.. Fields: Name: Robot code / AGV identifier (e.g. 1555058).; State: Robot state enum (Tipper/Hospital/Charger/Sorter/GLD/ShutDown family). Observed live values include SWaitingInzone, Removed, SWaitingForExchange, GoCharge, MovingToChargerEntranceQueue, MovingToTipperQueue.; ToteId: Tote currently

ontology_evidence.title: WCS model — HospitalDatabaseModel

source_refs.note: PascalCase model inventory; live query screenshot on p.75 supplied real column names (Name/EntranceId/DropOffId/InductionId/ExitId/Disabled)

ontology_evidence.text: Model HospitalDatabaseModel (robotics): Stores the hospitals and their entrance and exit queue locations as well as the drop-off and induction locations; this is where the AGV drops off a tote and picks one up.. Fields: Name: Hospital name, e.g. Hospital1.; EntranceId: Hospital entrance queue location.; DropOffId: Hospital tote drop-off location id (location FK) — where the AGV drops off a tote.; InductionId: Hospital tote induction location id (location FK) — where the AGV picks a tote back up.

nodes.diagnostic_interpretation: Observable pairing/routing confirmation is incomplete without readable RMS/WCS corroboration; use this node only to classify the site-reported pattern as confirmed vs not confirmed vs inconclusive.

nodes.intent: Determine whether RMS shows an abnormal robot membership, mapping, or status condition that could explain the pairing failure.
nodes.goal: Determine whether RMS shows an abnormal robot membership, mapping, or status condition that could explain the pairing failure.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet or robot status view for roster membership, mapping, location, and exception indicators associated with the affected workflow, and to interpret whether the displayed state is consistent with normal pairing.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source identifies RMS as the system used to view robot status and states that a removed robot was shown as not mapped; the artifact shows red-highlighted RMS table entries.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet or robot status view for roster membership, mapping, location, and exception indicators associated with the affected workflow, and to interpret whether the displayed state is consistent with normal pairing.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator or L1 support inspects the RMS fleet or robot status view. Healthy means the relevant robot membership, mapping, and status appear consistent with the intended operating area; unhealthy means a robot is shown as not mapped, missing, duplicated, abnormal, or highlighted as an exception; inconclusive means the RMS view is unreadable, unavailable, or does not identify the relevant robot state.

nodes.primary_action: Check RMS fleet/robot roster and mapping state for the affected workflow to determine whether the roster membership/mapping is abnormal and consistent with the reported pairing failure and hospital-lane routing pattern.

nodes.healthy_interpretation: RMS shows relevant robot membership/mapping consistent with the intended operating area and no remaining relevant exception/unmapped indicator.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: RMS shows relevant robot(s) as not mapped, missing, duplicated, exception-highlighted, or otherwise inconsistent with the affected workflow.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: RMS view is unreadable/unavailable or abnormal entry cannot be correlated with the affected workflow.

optional_corroboration.note: Because roster/mapping is being diagnosed, corroborate with the authoritative WCS/SSMS backend evidence for live robot location/roster state when possible (do not rely on unreadable RMS red highlights alone).

linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Corroborate live robot/AGV state and location/destination fields in the backend (authoritative for roster/mapping state).
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: Node intent is to verify device roster/mapping state; backend mapping provided uses RobotDatabaseModel to interpret live robot state/location/destination. This SSMS procedure is the closest on-topic AGV state inspection runbook in the candidate list.

nodes.generated_guidance: In this node, keep the interpretation strictly evidence-based. If RMS indicates “not mapped” or other abnormal roster/mapping indicators, proceed to the authorized isolation/removal step. If RMS is unreadable or the abnormal entry cannot be correlated to the affected workflow, stop and escalate via node_5 rather than performing physical actions.

ontology_evidence.title: WCS model — CellCodeDatabaseModel
ontology_evidence.text: Model CellCodeDatabaseModel (robotics): Stores all cell codes in the map. When a new AGV is added to the system while in a running state, the system first checks if the AGV's current cell code is in a missing zone under the sorter; if not, it uses this table to look up which hospital the cell code is connected to and sends an Initialize command to Geek.. ontology_evidence.text: Model RobotDatabaseModel (robotics): Robot/AGV live state: contains the data for every robot in the system including its state, tote name, assigned sorter side, current/destination location, and state.. ontology_evidence.text: Model LatticeCodeModel (geek_agv): Stores the lattice codes and their respective station IDs; when a tote is inducted or dropped off, Geek requires a lattice code for the location, and the Geek Comm module uses this table to convert the StationId from a robotics-module request into the lattice code Geek requires.. branches.condition_label: RMS indicates an unmapped, abnormal, or inconsistent robot roster/mapping state
branches.condition_descriptor: RMS shows not mapped/exception-highlighted or otherwise inconsistent robot roster/mapping relevant to the affected workflow.

branches.condition_label: RMS shows a normal relevant roster/mapping state or suspected pattern is not indicated
branches.condition_descriptor: No supported abnormal roster/mapping indication appears in RMS for the affected workflow.

branches.condition_label: RMS unreadable/uncoordinated evidence
branches.condition_descriptor: RMS cannot be read reliably or cannot be correlated to the affected workflow; avoid proceeding with physical removal based on ambiguity.

nodes.purpose: Determine whether RMS shows an abnormal robot membership, mapping, or status condition that could explain the pairing failure.
nodes.diagnostic_reasoning: The source identifies RMS as the system used to view robot status and states that a removed robot was shown as not mapped; the artifact shows red-highlighted RMS table entries.

evidence_collection_procedures.title: Check Selected Robot Details (Robot ID, Location, Node Code/Cell Code, Tote ID) in Robot Selection Overview
evidence_collection_procedures.purpose: Use the live RMS / fleet status UI Robot Selection Overview to select a robot and read its robot ID, location, node code (cell code), and tote presence/ID indicators—including the “?” tote mismatch case and the “layer_1” case when no tote is carried.

evidence_collection_procedures.title: Check Sorter-Side Charger Assignment in SSMS / Helix DB
evidence_collection_procedures.purpose: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) to inspect sorter-side and charger-assignment records. Confirm that the charger has a sorter-side model ID, that the charger is associated with the expected charging area or sorter side, and that its availability or disabled status is consistent with the investigation.

next_branches.condition_label: RMS indicates an unmapped, abnormal, or inconsistent robot roster/mapping state
next_branches.condition_descriptor: RMS shows not mapped/exception-highlighted or otherwise inconsistent robot roster/mapping relevant to the affected workflow.

next_branches.condition_label: RMS shows a normal relevant roster/mapping state or suspected pattern is not indicated
next_branches.condition_descriptor: No supported abnormal roster/mapping indication appears in RMS for the affected workflow.

next_branches.condition_label: RMS unreadable/uncoordinated evidence
next_branches.condition_descriptor: RMS cannot be read reliably or cannot be correlated to the affected workflow; avoid proceeding with physical removal based on ambiguity.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: RMS robot status tables show red-highlighted entries; exact values are unreadable.
Resolution details state that the removed robot was shown as not mapped.

linked_runbooks.title: Check Selected Robot Details (Robot ID, Location, Node Code/Cell Code, Tote ID) in Robot Selection Overview
linked_runbooks.purpose: Use the live RMS / fleet status UI Robot Selection Overview to select a robot and read its robot ID, location, node code (cell code), and tote presence/ID indicators—including the “?” tote mismatch case and the “layer_1” case when no tote is carried.

nodes.question: Determine whether RMS shows an abnormal robot membership, mapping, or status condition that could explain the pairing failure.

runbook_execution_result.success: You can identify the selected robot’s robot ID and location from the expanded Robot Selection Overview detail panel.
runbook_execution_result.failure: Detail section cannot be expanded (small arrow does not reveal details).

node_interpretation_mapping.failure: Abnormal robot roster/mapping state indicated (e.g., unmapped robot).
node_interpretation_mapping.inconclusive: Cannot read RMS or correlate the abnormal entry to the affected workflow.

nodes.title: Use an authorized site-side robot isolation or removal path
nodes.intent: If an abnormal roster or mapping condition is supported, use the approved site procedure to isolate or remove the affected robot from the operating system and place it in a safe non-operational state.
nodes.goal: If an abnormal roster or mapping condition is supported, use the approved site procedure to isolate or remove the affected robot from the operating system and place it in a safe non-operational state.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed for authorized site-side AGV physical isolation and system removal, including safety prerequisites, handling of a robot in an abnormal location, charger placement, and confirmation of the corresponding RMS state; exact removal or handling steps belong in the runbook.
nodes.source_supported_description: The incident reports site-side removal of a robot from the system and placement on a charger, followed by reported system recovery.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for authorized site-side AGV physical isolation and system removal, including safety prerequisites, handling of a robot in an abnormal location, charger placement, and confirmation of the corresponding RMS state; exact removal or handling steps belong in the runbook.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The authorized site operator observes that the identified robot has been removed or isolated from active operation and placed in the reported safe state, such as charging, without creating a new physical hazard. Successful completion is confirmed by the site; failure or uncertainty means the robot cannot be safely isolated, the system-side state is unclear, or the action is outside the executor's authorization.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The source includes RMS screenshots and a visible note that the site removed a robot from the system (case_228723:page_6).

ontology_gaps: The packet does not specify the approved remove/add procedure, authorization boundary, or exact system-side confirmation criteria.
healthy_indicators: Authorized site personnel confirm the affected robot is safely isolated and no longer participating in active operation.
unhealthy_indicators: The robot remains active, obstructed, or associated with the abnormal roster state.
The system continues to exhibit the pairing failure after the supported isolation action.
inconclusive_indicators: The site cannot confirm the robot's physical state or the corresponding RMS state.
The source-supported action cannot be performed safely or by an authorized role.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Stop if physical access, safety conditions, authorization, or system-side state cannot be confirmed.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Site removed the robot from the system, placed it on a charger, and reported that the system began functioning again.

nodes.primary_action: If RMS indicates abnormal roster/mapping, coordinate with authorized site personnel to isolate or remove the affected robot from active operation and place it in a safe non-operational state (e.g., charging), then confirm the corresponding RMS state.
evidence_to_collect: Safety/authorization confirmation that the site executor is allowed to isolate/remove the affected robot
Confirmation the identified robot is no longer participating in active operation and is placed in the reported safe state (e.g., charging)
RMS-side confirmation that the corresponding robot roster state changed as expected after isolation/removal
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Authorized site personnel confirm the affected robot is safely isolated/non-operational and no longer associated with the abnormal roster state.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Robot remains active/obstructed or still associated with the abnormal roster state; pairing failure continues after isolation/removal.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Site cannot confirm physical state or corresponding RMS state; action cannot be performed safely/authorized.

optional_corroboration.note: If roster/mapping evidence is uncertain or RMS cannot be confirmed, do not proceed with physical actions—use escalation gate.

nodes.title: Confirm pairing and operational stability
nodes.intent: Determine whether the affected workflow has recovered after the authorized robot isolation or removal action.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the affected workflow has recovered after the authorized robot isolation or removal action.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate pairing availability through site observation and to review the RMS fleet or robot status view for persistent abnormal membership, mapping, or exception indicators during a defined monitoring period.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports that the system began functioning after robot removal and remained operational during approximately ten minutes of monitoring, while acknowledging that the recovery was not independently validated by readable RMS data.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate pairing availability through site observation and to review the RMS fleet or robot status view for persistent abnormal membership, mapping, or exception indicators during a defined monitoring period.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator confirms that the affected workflow can obtain a pair and that AMRs are operating as expected; where available, the operator or L1 support checks the RMS fleet view for the abnormal entry to be absent or no longer active. Healthy means pairing resumes and operation remains stable during observation; unhealthy means pairing remains unavailable, AMRs continue routing abnormally, or the abnormal RMS state persists; inconclusive means recovery is only reported administratively or the RMS details cannot be read.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The source reports that the site believed the system was working and that support remained on the call to monitor it (case_228723:page_7).
The recovery evidence includes embedded RMS screenshots associated with the report that the system remained operational (case_228723:page_10).

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The source uses RMS screenshots and reports continued operation after robot removal, but does not provide independently readable final roster values.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not define a validated live RMS success state or an independent telemetry-based recovery check.
healthy_indicators: Site confirms that the affected workflow can obtain a pair.
AMRs no longer uniformly route to the hospital lane.
RMS no longer shows the relevant abnormal roster or mapping indication.
Operation remains stable during monitoring.
unhealthy_indicators: The affected workflow still cannot obtain a pair.
AMRs continue routing to the hospital lane unexpectedly.
RMS continues to show a relevant unmapped or abnormal robot state.
inconclusive_indicators: Recovery is stated only in a case comment or message without direct operational confirmation.
The RMS screenshots do not show readable final status details.
The system works briefly but stable monitoring is not completed.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Site believed removal may have fixed the issue and support monitored operation.
System reportedly began functioning again and remained operational during approximately ten minutes of monitoring.

nodes.primary_action: Validate pairing availability and operational stability after the authorized isolation/removal by confirming the affected workflow can obtain a pair and that AMR routing returns to intended behavior; corroborate with RMS and backend roster/mapping state where readable.
evidence_to_collect: Site confirmation during monitoring window that the affected workflow can obtain a pair
Site confirmation that AMRs route as intended (not diverted unexpectedly to hospital lane)
RMS confirmation that the previously abnormal roster/mapping indication is absent or no longer active (when readable)
Record duration of monitoring window and whether stability persisted
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Pairing resumes, intended routing returns, and operation remains stable during monitoring; RMS no longer shows relevant abnormal roster/mapping indicator.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Pairing remains unavailable; AMRs continue abnormal routing; abnormal RMS roster/mapping indication persists during monitoring.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Recovery is only stated administratively (no operational confirmation), RMS screenshots/details are unreadable, or monitoring window is not completed.

optional_corroboration.note: For roster/mapping stability validation, corroborate with backend WCS/SSMS live robot state/location evidence to ensure RMS is not stale.

linked_primary_procedure.title: WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) AGV state inspection
linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Backend corroboration of live AGV state/location/destination and roster state after the physical isolation/removal action.
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: Node type is validation gate on roster/mapping recovery; the strongest available backend corroboration candidate is the AGV state inspection SSMS procedure.
match_gaps: No node-specific “monitoring window / validation gate” runbook present; link chosen for backend corroboration of roster/mapping stability.

nodes.generated_guidance: Do not close the case based on one-time site statements. Confirm pairing and routing stability during a defined monitoring period and ensure the abnormal roster/mapping state is no longer present (or clearly deactivated).

ontology_evidence.text: Model CellCodeDatabaseModel (robotics): Stores all cell codes in the map. When a new AGV is added to the system while in a running state, the system first checks if the AGV's current cell code is in a missing zone under the sorter; if not, it uses this table to look up which hospital the cell code is connected to and sends an Initialize command to Geek.. structured_payload.title: Zone pairing failure with abnormal AMR routing or roster state
structured_payload.user_facing_summary: Use when a site reports that a zone cannot obtain a pair, AMRs are not behaving as expected, or replacement AMRs are routing to the hospital instead of supporting the affected workflow.
structured_payload.playbook_goal: Confirm the observable pairing and fleet symptoms, determine whether the affected AMR roster or mapping state is abnormal, guide an authorized site-side isolation or removal decision when supported, and validate that normal operation returns.
observed_entry_symptoms: A zone is unable to get a pair.
The ACB workflow is reported as down or unable to operate.

An AMR is reported with low battery or is physically under a rack.
The site reports that AMR behavior remains abnormal after an attempted replacement.

structured_payload.confidence_reason: The packet contains a clear observable symptom pattern, a named RMS surface, repeated discussion of remove/add and mapping state, a source-supported site-side recovery action, and reported post-action stability. Confidence is limited because the RMS details are partly unreadable, the recovery was narrative rather than independently verified, and the source uses inconsistent ACB/ECB naming.

nodes.title: Confirm zone pairing failure and abnormal AMR behavior
nodes.intent: Determine whether the reported issue is an active zone pairing failure accompanied by abnormal AMR routing or inability to support the affected workflow.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the reported issue is an active zone pairing failure accompanied by abnormal AMR routing or inability to support the affected workflow.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to confirm with the site whether the affected zone is currently unable to get a pair, whether AMRs are routing to the hospital lane instead of the expected workflow, whether a low-battery or physically obstructed AMR is involved, and whether RMS shows the same abnormal fleet or pairing presentation; use generic affected-zone and reported-robot references rather than incident-specific identifiers.
nodes.source_supported_description: The site reported inability to get a pair, AMRs going to the hospital, and an earlier low-battery AMR condition. RMS artifacts show status tables with abnormal-looking red entries, but exact values are unreadable.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to confirm with the site whether the affected zone is currently unable to get a pair, whether AMRs are routing to the hospital lane instead of the expected workflow, whether a low-battery or physically obstructed AMR is involved, and whether RMS shows the same abnormal fleet or pairing presentation; use generic affected-zone and reported-robot references rather than incident-specific identifiers.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site or L1 support observes the affected zone behavior through site interview and, when available, the RMS fleet or status view. Healthy or alternate signal: the zone can obtain a pair and AMRs route to the expected workflow. Unhealthy signal: the zone cannot obtain a pair, AMRs consistently route to the hospital, or the site reports an AMR unable to support the workflow. Inconclusive: the report is intermittent, the affected workflow cannot be reproduced, or the RMS view is unavailable or unreadable.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Support messages record direct phone discussion with the site about inability to get a pair, low battery, replacement AMRs, and hospital routing; source refs case_228723:page_1 and case_228723:page_2.
The page 6 artifact is visibly an RMS web UI with robot or system status tables and red-highlighted entries; source ref case_228723:page_6.

relevant_evidence: The source discusses AMR add/remove handling, possible roster problems, and abnormal RMS status.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology snippet does not establish a specific backend mapping for zone pairing state or hospital-lane routing for this node.
healthy_indicators: Site reports that the affected zone can obtain a pair.
AMRs are observed supporting the expected workflow rather than uniformly routing to the hospital.
RMS presents a consistent normal fleet state without the reported abnormal entries.
unhealthy_indicators: Site reports that the affected zone cannot obtain a pair.
Multiple or replacement AMRs route to the hospital lane.
A low-battery or physically constrained AMR is reported in the affected area.
RMS shows exception-style or red-highlighted robot status entries.
inconclusive_indicators: The site cannot reproduce the pairing failure.
Only one ambiguous AMR symptom is reported without confirming zone impact.
RMS is unavailable or the relevant table details cannot be read.

nodes.primary_action: Confirm with the site (via interview) whether the affected zone is currently unable to obtain a pair and whether AMRs are currently routing to the hospital lane; then compare against RMS fleet/status presentation to determine if the behavior is currently active vs intermittent/unreadable.
nodes.primary_surface: site_interview + RMS (RMS UI evidence when readable)
evidence_to_collect: Site confirmation of current pair availability/unavailability for the affected zone (current, not historical).
Site confirmation of current AMR routing behavior (expected workflow vs routing to hospital lane).
Whether a low-battery or physically obstructed AMR is currently present in/near the affected zone (confirm it as a current condition).
RMS evidence that matches the symptom timeframe: whether the fleet/robot status tables show abnormal entries relevant to pairing/hospital routing (values must be readable enough to interpret).
If RMS cannot be read/verified, capture that limitation explicitly (unreadable table/fields).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: The affected zone can obtain a pair, and AMRs are not consistently diverted to the hospital lane; RMS (when readable) does not show consistent abnormal status entries matching the report.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: The affected zone cannot obtain a pair and AMRs consistently route to the hospital lane (or site reports AMRs unable to support the affected workflow); RMS (when readable) shows abnormal/exception-style robot/system state consistent with the report.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: The report is intermittent/not reproducible on demand, RMS is unavailable or unreadable (cannot interpret relevant fields), or the site cannot provide enough evidence to confirm current pairing and routing behavior.

optional_corroboration.note: If the evidence suggests active faults, corroborate the symptom using WCS/SSMS AGV state inspection (robot_location_state / RobotDatabaseModel) before pursuing roster/mapping recovery decisions.

If hospital diversion is prominent, the backend hospital_diversion evidence (HospitalDatabaseModel / HospitalTagsModel / CellCodeDatabaseModel correlation) should be treated as the authoritative corroboration, but only if a matching runbook exists in the candidate list.

linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Inspect authoritative AGV live state (including location/state fields) to corroborate whether abnormal roster/location behavior aligns with reported pairing failure and hospital diversion.
match_gaps: The node requires evidence about zone pairing and hospital-lane routing, but the available SSMS candidate is an AGV state inspection (not a dedicated zone pairing/hospital-routing SQL).
No explicit runbook candidate provided for hospital_diversion SQL evidence for this node; link is therefore a partial match via shared robot_location_state evidence.
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: Highest-confidence SSMS backend candidate for authoritative robot_location_state-style evidence; aligns to the ontology’s required evidence concept device_roster_state/robot_location_state even though the procedure is not explicitly zone-pair/hospital-routing specific.

nodes.generated_guidance: Ask the site to confirm (1) zone pairing failure is current, (2) AMRs are currently diverted to hospital lane vs supporting the workflow, and (3) whether the low-battery/physical obstruction condition is current—not merely a possible initiator. Then use RMS only if the relevant status tables/fields are readable enough to interpret; otherwise record the unreadability as a first-class gap and route to escalation/retriage as appropriate.

ontology_evidence.title: WCS model — CellCodeDatabaseModel
ontology_evidence.text: Model CellCodeDatabaseModel (robotics): Stores all cell codes in the map. When a new AGV is added to the system while in a running state, the system first checks if the AGV's current cell code is in a missing zone under the sorter; if not, it uses this table to look up which hospital the cell code is connected to and sends an Initialize command to Geek.. nodes.title: Determine whether AMR roster or mapping state is abnormal
nodes.intent: Determine whether recent AMR replacement or remove/add activity left an AMR missing, unmapped, incorrectly rostered, or otherwise unable to receive the expected task.
nodes.goal: Determine whether recent AMR replacement or remove/add activity left an AMR missing, unmapped, incorrectly rostered, or otherwise unable to receive the expected task.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet or robot status view for the affected AMR's roster membership, mapped or unmapped indication, location, and assignment-related abnormal state, and to compare the displayed state with the site's reported remove/add history without relying on incident-specific robot identifiers.
nodes.source_supported_description: Support discussion proposed improper remove/add or RMS rostering as a possible explanation. Resolution text states that a robot was shown as not mapped, but the source does not prove that this was the confirmed root cause.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet or robot status view for the affected AMR's roster membership, mapped or unmapped indication, location, and assignment-related abnormal state, and to compare the displayed state with the site's reported remove/add history without relying on incident-specific robot identifiers.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site or L1 support observes the RMS roster or robot status view. Healthy signal: affected AMRs appear as expected members of the fleet with consistent mapped or assigned state and no relevant exception indication. Unhealthy signal: an AMR is absent, shown as not mapped, has an abnormal roster state, or does not receive the expected task after replacement or remove/add activity. Inconclusive: the RMS view is too unclear to identify the relevant state, or the site history does not establish which AMR was replaced or added.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Support discussion explicitly refers to robots being properly rostered in RMS, and the artifact shows RMS status tables; source refs case_228723:page_2, case_228723:page_5, and case_228723:page_6.

relevant_evidence: The source explicitly raises improper remove/add handling, RMS rostering, and a robot shown as not mapped.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology snippet does not provide a specific backend field mapping for task assignment eligibility or zone pairing correlation.
healthy_indicators: The relevant AMR is present in the expected RMS roster.
The AMR is shown with a normal mapped or assigned state.
The AMR's displayed location and assignment state are consistent with the site's reported physical state.
unhealthy_indicators: The AMR is shown as not mapped or otherwise absent from the expected roster.
The displayed roster or mapping state conflicts with the physical or site-reported state.
The AMR remains unable to receive the expected task after replacement or add activity.
inconclusive_indicators: The RMS screenshot does not expose readable identifiers or status meanings.
The site cannot identify the affected AMR or the sequence of replacement activity.
The displayed state is abnormal but cannot be linked to the pairing symptom.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Support suggested robots may not have been removed and added properly and referred to RMS rostering.
RMS status tables with red-highlighted entries; exact status values are not readable.
Resolution details state that a removed robot was shown as not mapped.

nodes.primary_action: Inspect RMS fleet/robot status presentation to determine whether an AMR roster/mapping state is abnormal and consistent with the site’s remove/add or replacement history (e.g., an AMR absent, shown as not mapped, or otherwise unable to receive expected tasks).
nodes.primary_surface: RMS / AGV status UI (fleet/robot roster/mapping view) + site interview context
evidence_to_collect: Whether the affected AMR(s) are present in the expected RMS roster/fleet list.
Whether any AMR is shown as not mapped/absent or has abnormal roster/mapping state.
Whether the shown location/assignment state in RMS is consistent with the site-reported physical condition and remove/add history.
RMS screenshot readability: whether identifiers/status meanings are interpretable; record unreadable limitations explicitly.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: The relevant AMRs are present as expected and shown with normal mapped/assigned state; RMS location/assignment aligns with the site physical state; no mapping anomaly persists after the remove/add activity.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: An AMR is absent from expected roster, shown as not mapped or otherwise abnormal roster/mapping state, and that abnormal state is associated with the pairing symptom; persistence remains after the site’s replacement/remove/add activity.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: RMS evidence is too unclear/unreadable to identify the relevant AMR or interpret status meanings; site cannot identify the affected AMR(s) or provide an adequate sequence linking to RMS state; mapping anomalies cannot be linked to the symptom.

optional_corroboration.note: If an abnormal roster/mapping state appears likely, corroborate using WCS/SSMS robot live state evidence (RobotDatabaseModel/RobotLocationDatabaseModel fields) before directing any fleet-state isolation/removal action.

linked_primary_procedure.title: WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) AGV state inspection
linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Corroborate whether the robot roster/mapping anomaly suggested by RMS is reflected in authoritative robot state (state/current/destination/location fields).
match_gaps: Node requires roster/mapping inspection specifically in RMS; the chosen SSMS procedure is a general AGV state inspection rather than a dedicated RMS roster/mapping crosswalk.
No dedicated SSMS 'not mapped' mapping-state procedure was provided in candidates.
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: Authoritative backend corroboration aligns to ontology’s device_roster_state/robot_location_state evidence required for confidence before proceeding.

nodes.generated_guidance: Use RMS only to establish whether a roster/mapping anomaly exists and whether it plausibly explains the pairing failure. Do not assume low battery or hospital routing is the confirmed root cause; treat it as context until RMS/SSMS confirm which AMR/location state is abnormal. If RMS is unreadable, treat as inconclusive and do not proceed to fleet-state recovery.

ontology_evidence.title: WCS model — CellCodeDatabaseModel
ontology_evidence.text: Model CellCodeDatabaseModel (robotics): Stores all cell codes in the map. When a new AGV is added to the system while in a running state, the system first checks if the AGV's current cell code is in a missing zone under the sorter; if not, it uses this table to look up which hospital the cell code is connected to and sends an Initialize command to Geek.. ontology_evidence.text: Model RobotDatabaseModel (robotics): Robot/AGV live state: contains the data for every robot in the system including its state, tote name, assigned sorter side, current/destination location, and state.. ontology_evidence.text: Model LatticeCodeModel (geek_agv): Stores the lattice codes and their respective station IDs; when a tote is inducted or dropped off, Geek requires a lattice code for the location, and the Geek Comm module uses this table to convert the StationId from a robotics-module request into the lattice code Geek requires.. nodes.source_supported_description: The source records site-side removal of a robot from the system and placement on charger after discussion of roster and mapping concerns. It does not provide a complete or repeatable removal/add procedure.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to apply the decision rubric for an AMR shown as unmapped or incorrectly rostered, including comparison of RMS state with site physical confirmation and the safety and authorization criteria for any site-side isolation or remove-from-system action; do not encode exact remove/add steps here.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site or L1 support compares the RMS roster or mapping indication with the physical and reported AMR state. Recovery-path signal: a specific AMR is shown or reported as unmapped, incorrectly rostered, or otherwise associated with the pairing failure, and an authorized site role can safely isolate it. Alternate signal: the roster or mapping state appears normal, the issue is not linked to one AMR, or the site cannot safely perform the supported action. Inconclusive: the evidence is contradictory or the relevant RMS state cannot be established.

evidence_to_collect: Identify the specific AMR (by site-reported physical reference and/or RMS identifiers) that is associated with the abnormal mapping/roster state.
Confirm RMS shows the AMR as unmapped/abnormal in a way that matches the symptom.
Site confirms physical state of the AMR (e.g., present/available vs constrained/out of service) and can access it safely if isolation/remove is needed.
Authorization/safety prerequisites are present for the site-side isolation/remove action (do not proceed if missing).
If evidence is contradictory or cannot link AMR to symptom, record as inconclusive.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Evidence links the abnormal roster/mapping state to a specific AMR and an authorized site role can safely isolate it from active fleet participation using approved criteria.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: The evidence links an unmapped/incorrectly rostered AMR to the symptom and the site confirms the ability to safely isolate/remove it (appropriate holding/charging state can be established).
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: RMS mapping evidence cannot be established/readable, AMR cannot be linked to the symptom, or safety/authorization prerequisites are not confirmed.

optional_corroboration.note: Before authorizing isolation/removal, corroborate the AMR’s authoritative state/location in SSMS (robot_location_state) when available and when it matches the evidence path—do not fabricate a physical-action justification from unreadable RMS alone.

nodes.generated_guidance: This node is a decision rubric gate, not the execution step. Only proceed when (1) a specific AMR is evidenced as unmapped/incorrectly rostered and linked to the pairing failure and hospital-routing symptom, and (2) the site role is authorized and can safely place that AMR into a charging/holding state. If those prerequisites are absent, route to escalation gate.

ontology_evidence.title: WCS model — CellCodeDatabaseModel
ontology_evidence.text: Model CellCodeDatabaseModel (robotics): Stores all cell codes in the map. When a new AGV is added to the system while in a running state, the system first checks if the AGV's current cell code is in a missing zone under the sorter; if not, it uses this table to look up which hospital the cell code is connected to and sends an Initialize command to Geek.. nodes.question: Choose whether the affected AMR should remain isolated from the active fleet under an authorized site procedure, or whether the evidence does not support that path.

node_interpretation_mapping.success: No supported fleet-state recovery path based on unmapped/incorrectly rostered AMR evidence.
node_interpretation_mapping.failure: Supported path exists: a specific AMR can be safely isolated/removed by authorized site action.
node_interpretation_mapping.inconclusive: Evidence is contradictory or missing required prerequisites for the fleet-state action.

nodes.title: Perform authorized AMR isolation or removal action
nodes.intent: Carry out the source-supported high-level recovery action when the affected AMR is linked to the abnormal roster or mapping state and the authorized site procedure permits it.
nodes.goal: Carry out the source-supported high-level recovery action when the affected AMR is linked to the abnormal roster or mapping state and the authorized site procedure permits it.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed for authorized site-side AMR isolation or removal from active system participation, including physical safety prerequisites, charging or holding-state requirements, RMS state confirmation, and role limits; the procedure must define the approved remove/add handling without embedding exact operational steps here.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source-supported recovery was site removal of an AMR from the system followed by placement on charger. The source does not document exact steps and does not establish that this action is universally appropriate.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for authorized site-side AMR isolation or removal from active system participation, including physical safety prerequisites, charging or holding-state requirements, RMS state confirmation, and role limits; the procedure must define the approved remove/add handling without embedding exact operational steps here.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The authorized site role observes that the affected AMR has been removed from active system participation and placed in a safe charging or holding state, consistent with the source-reported recovery action. Progress signal: the AMR is no longer contributing to the abnormal pairing behavior. Unsuccessful signal: the AMR remains active in the problematic state or the site cannot complete the authorized action. Inconclusive: the action is reported but the resulting RMS or operational state cannot be confirmed.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The source reports removal from the system and includes RMS screenshots showing robot status tables; source refs case_228723:page_6 and case_228723:page_10.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology does not provide a complete cataloged procedure for the specific remove-from-system action described in the incident.
healthy_indicators: The authorized site role confirms the affected AMR is isolated from active operation.
The AMR is confirmed in the intended charging or holding state.
RMS no longer presents the AMR as contributing to the abnormal pairing condition.
unhealthy_indicators: The AMR remains active in the problematic fleet state.
The site cannot place the AMR in a safe holding or charging state.
The pairing symptom continues immediately after the authorized action.
inconclusive_indicators: Only the physical action is reported without a corresponding system-state confirmation.
The site cannot confirm which AMR was isolated.
RMS status remains unreadable or contradictory.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Stop if physical safety, authorization, or approved remove/add prerequisites are not satisfied. Do not substitute this node for the exact site procedure.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Site removed a robot from the system, placed it on charger, and reported that the system began functioning again.
Resolution details report removal of a robot shown as not mapped.

nodes.primary_action: Carry out the authorized site-side AMR isolation/removal action for the specific unmapped/incorrectly rostered AMR and place it into a safe charging/holding state, then confirm the AMR is no longer contributing to the abnormal pairing behavior.
nodes.primary_surface: RMS and/or Hospital HMI + physical access (site execution of approved procedure)
evidence_to_collect: Site confirms the selected AMR has been removed from active fleet participation.
Site confirms placement into the intended safe charging/holding state.
RMS evidence that the AMR no longer appears as contributing to the abnormal pairing behavior (or note inability to confirm due to readability/availability).
If unsuccessful, record whether the AMR remains active in the problematic state.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: The authorized site role confirms the affected AMR is isolated from active operation and in the intended charging/holding state; RMS no longer presents the AMR as contributing to the abnormal pairing behavior.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: The AMR remains active in the problematic fleet state or the site cannot complete placement into a safe holding/charging state; pairing symptom persists immediately after the action.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Action is reported, but system-state confirmation in RMS is missing/unreadable/contradictory.

optional_corroboration.note: After isolation/removal, validate restored behavior using node_5 (short monitoring) before closing the troubleshooting path.

linked_primary_procedure.title: Recover a Faulted AGV Carrying a Tote (RMS stop → Hospital HMI remove → re-add → resume RMS)
linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Provide an approved recovery procedure family for removing a faulted AMR from RMS/Hospital participation and resuming RMS once safe; used only if the incident’s conditions align with procedure scope.
match_gaps: The node/source specifically describes 'removed from the system and placed on charger' after mapping/roster concerns; the linked candidate procedure is a broader 'faulted AGV carrying a tote' recovery path.
The packet does not provide a dedicated 'not mapped robot remove/add' procedure; this is a partial-match recovery candidate family.
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: Closest available recovery-family candidate in retrieval for moving an AGV through RMS/Hospital remove/resume steps; however, scope mismatch risk is high given the incident’s described high-level action without tote/fault specifics.

nodes.generated_guidance: Only perform the approved remove/add/isolation action if the site’s authorization and prerequisites from node_3 are met. Execute the recovery action at the site using the candidate’s approved workflow (RMS/Hospital-side), then confirm the AMR is in a safe charging/holding state and no longer contributing to the abnormal pairing symptom in RMS. If you cannot confirm state (unreadable/contradictory evidence), treat as inconclusive and proceed to node_5 or escalation as dictated by validation gate outcomes.

nodes.title: Validate restored pairing and stable AMR operation
nodes.intent: Confirm that the affected workflow has recovered after the authorized fleet-state action and remains operational during observation.
nodes.goal: Confirm that the affected workflow has recovered after the authorized fleet-state action and remains operational during observation.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate the affected zone's pairing behavior through site observation, confirm expected AMR routing and fleet state in RMS, and define a short stability-monitoring period before declaring recovery; include criteria for failed validation and evidence capture without prescribing exact screen navigation.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports that operation resumed after robot removal and remained operational during approximately 10 minutes of monitoring, while acknowledging that the recovery was reported rather than independently confirmed by readable live RMS details.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate the affected zone's pairing behavior through site observation, confirm expected AMR routing and fleet state in RMS, and define a short stability-monitoring period before declaring recovery; include criteria for failed validation and evidence capture without prescribing exact screen navigation.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site observes the affected workflow and, when available, checks RMS status. Healthy signal: the zone can obtain a pair, AMRs resume expected operation rather than uniformly routing to the hospital, and the system remains operational during a short monitoring period. Unhealthy signal: pairing remains unavailable, AMRs continue abnormal hospital routing, or the same roster or mapping symptom returns. Inconclusive: recovery is reported but no direct operational observation or readable RMS confirmation is available.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The source reports that the site believed the system had begun working and that support remained on the call to monitor operation; source refs case_228723:page_7 and case_228723:page_10.
The page 10 artifact contains embedded RMS screenshots associated with the reported recovery, although detailed status values are not readable; source ref case_228723:page_10.

relevant_evidence: The source uses RMS screenshots and reports continued operation after removal of the affected AMR.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology snippet does not establish a specific backend validation mapping for pair acquisition or hospital-lane routing.

AMRs resume the expected workflow instead of consistently routing to the hospital.

unhealthy_indicators: The zone remains unable to get a pair.
AMRs continue routing abnormally to the hospital.
The same or another fleet-state anomaly reappears during monitoring.
The reported recovery cannot be reproduced by the site.
inconclusive_indicators: Recovery is based only on a case note or message without direct site observation.
The monitoring period is too short to assess stability.
RMS screenshots or status views are unavailable or unreadable.

ontology_evidence.title: WCS model — CellCodeDatabaseModel
ontology_evidence.text: Model CellCodeDatabaseModel (robotics): Stores all cell codes in the map. When a new AGV is added to the system while in a running state, the system first checks if the AGV's current cell code is in a missing zone under the sorter; if not, it uses this table to look up which hospital the cell code is connected to and sends an Initialize command to Geek.. evidence_collection_procedures.purpose: Use the RMS / fleet status UI map to verify which tote number is currently associated with a specific rack location. evidence_collection_procedures.purpose: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) live read-only database surface to inspect robotics-related AGV state records when the RMS / fleet status UI reports AGVs out of sync or the robotic system is stopped.
